receipt_result.interpretation: Allocated <= logical is not universal, even for .pt files. 128 KiB is an observed additive envelope only, not a demonstrated allocation unit or worst-case bound for future active writes. Recorded dev=80 on capture hosts is not proof of future mount/server configuration. Comparable terminal timing aggregates do support allocated <= logical for all 96 observed shards; this does not contradict individual-file positive excesses in the storage captures or establish an all-times bound.

no_double_counting: For an all-times allocation model A <= sum(logical lengths)+N*q+C and an 8 GiB bound that includes the active reservation, buffered/unflushed serialized bytes are already counted. Adding min(M,8 GiB) again is conservative double counting and unnecessary for that global model. This statement does not dismiss separate server metadata, transient extents, preallocation, rewrite/copy amplification or untracked writes; these require their own admitted terms. A threshold watchdog uses a different measured-prefix plus future-growth model and cannot inherit the global proof before its premises are established.

remaining_blockers.required: Bind an actual finite allocation upper bound to this destination and exact write behavior, including active/preallocated/delayed blocks, directory and backend overhead, or use verified enforcement with bounded overshoot. Existing accepted stat receipts alone do not bound unseen/transient peaks. A universally hard quota is not the only acceptable mechanism.

Implement and review prospective file/entry creation limits and all controls/log/partial/error-write bounds. 4096 is proposed, not enforced; the existing 100000 observation ceiling is not pre-admission. Account for directory st_blocks omitted by current file_stats and for every byte outside the logical writer guard. With q=128 KiB and C=2 GiB, 4096 files conditionally yield 10.5 GiB, while 100000 yield 22.20703125 GiB.

If watchdog overshoot is used for admission, prove actual cgroup configuration/membership, its finite allowance including any transient excess, a worst-case NFS allocation rate or write quantum, bounded observation staleness and effective stop delay, in-flight/server pending allocations and all writer cessation. An observed throughput average is not a worst-case burst cap; SIGSTOP intent is not confirmed completion/cancellation. Current M=128 GiB additive case is 138.5 GiB before bandwidth; L=7 GiB,D=8 GiB,q*N=0.5 GiB,C=2 GiB leaves only 0.5 GiB for all rate/delay/other effects.
